events.title: Slavery Ends in the District of Columbia
events.description: President Abraham Lincoln signed the District of Columbia Compensated Emancipation Act, which abolished slavery in the nation's capital. It freed enslaved people there and offered compensation to their owners.
events.significance: It was the first time the federal government freed enslaved people by law. It came months before the Emancipation Proclamation.

events.title: Charlie Chaplin Is Born
events.description: Charles Spencer Chaplin was born in London. He rose from a childhood of poverty to become one of cinema's first global superstars. His Little Tramp character was known around the world.
events.significance: Chaplin helped turn silent film into a major art form. He was an actor, director, producer and composer.

events.title: Lenin Returns to Russia
events.description: Vladimir Lenin arrived in Petrograd after years in exile. He came back as the Russian Revolution was underway.
events.significance: His return reshaped the revolution. Within months the Bolsheviks took power, and in 1922 the Soviet Union was founded with Lenin as its first leader.

events.title: Death of Rosalind Franklin
events.description: The English chemist Rosalind Franklin died at age 37. Her X-ray diffraction images of DNA, including the famous Photo 51, were key evidence for the molecule's structure.
events.significance: Her work was central to the discovery of the DNA double helix. Her contribution is now widely recognized as essential.

events.title: Ten Nations Join the European Union
events.description: The Treaty of Accession was signed in Athens. It admitted ten new members, including Poland, Cyprus and the Czech Republic.
events.significance: It was the largest single expansion in the EU's history. It helped reunite Europe after the Cold War divide.
